games.title: Beast of Reincarnation
games.summary: Unreal Engine 5 titles that crash on the first cutscene. The carrier sits under a compiler-named subfolder, which the script discovers rather than assumes.

excerpts.note: Electra asks the H.264 decoder for the types it can output; CrossOver's offers no NV12, so the fix puts NV12 back in the list.
Sets Electra.Win.H264UseOldOutputPath, found by its own name rather than by an address, so Electra takes its CPU buffer path and never the D3D one.

games.cause: Electra plays the H.264 video through a Media Foundation decoder that offers no NV12 on CrossOver, so the picture never reaches the screen.
games.symptom: Sound plays, picture never appears. No crash on a stock engine
games.fix: NV12 put back on the menu, and one console variable found by its own name. **No addresses any more**
games.crossover: Stable 26.3, on an engine carrying **winevideo**'s `winegstreamer`. A plain 26.3 stalls after two frames

games.title: CONTROL Resonant
games.summary: Hides the window-interior shader D3DMetal draws as flat colours.

excerpts.note: The pipeline whose pixel shader draws the lit rooms behind windows is created with its colour writes muted, from a copy of the game's description.
Zeroes the write mask of each of the eight render targets in the blend description.

games.symptom: Faces and hair render as black boxes; the lit rooms behind windows show as flat violet, cyan and yellow, spreading to neighbouring windows as the camera moves
games.cause: Faces: Metal 4 on. Windows: one pixel shader, `interiorPS`, whose non-uniform texture read D3DMetal runs as uniform, plus a second fault, outside the shaders, that shows up after about a minute of play
games.fix: Metal 4 off for this title; the pipelines built with `interiorPS` are created writing nothing
games.crossover: Stable 26.3 with Game Porting Toolkit 4.0b2 (2026-09-26)

games.title: Cyberpunk 2077
games.summary: Writes the one instruction that makes the game offer the MetalFX denoiser it ships, and signs its app again ad hoc. M3 or later.

credits.name: An anonymous community script
credits.note: The patch comes from it; MacGameFix writes one of its five words.

excerpts.note: The recipe for 2.5.0: the build, the executable's hash, the offset, the four bytes there (mov w0,#0) and the four written (mov w0,#1), and the hash after.

games.symptom: The MetalFX denoiser the Mac version ships (MTLFXTemporalDenoisedScaler) is never offered in the settings.
games.cause: The renderer answers "not supported" from a method of two instructions, `mov w0,#0; ret`.
games.fix: Four bytes of the executable: `mov w0,#1` over the first instruction, at the offset its build's row in `cp2077-denoiser.recipes` names, and the app signed again ad hoc. The original is kept aside.
games.backend: None: the macOS version 2.5.0 runs natively, on an M3 or later.

games.title: Devil May Cry 5
games.summary: Crashes when a VC-1 video plays; the fix decodes it itself where the engine cannot.

excerpts.note: When Media Foundation refuses a video (VC-1 in ASF, which no CrossOver decodes), the stream is handed to the fix's own ASF reader instead.

games.symptom: Crashes when a particular video plays. In Devil May Cry 5 it is the skill previews on the Customize screen
games.cause: The video is VC-1, and CrossOver ships no VC-1 decoder
games.fix: The fix's own VC-1 reader in the game folder (`install-re-vc1-fix.sh`); the staged codec still works and is used first where present
games.crossover: Stable 26.3 with the codec staged; CrossOver Preview 27 through NotProton with nothing staged (2026-10-14)

games.title: DYNASTY WARRIORS: ORIGINS
games.summary: The player needs D3D11 video interfaces D3DMetal lacks, and the decoded frame carried across to its D3D12 renderer.

excerpts.note: The D3D12 renderer opens the handle of a frame decoded on the D3D11 device; the bridge answers with a texture on the game's own device that carries the frame across.
On the D3D11 side IDXGIResource::GetSharedHandle returns E_NOTIMPL; the bridge hands out a handle of its own that the D3D12 side recognises.

games.symptom: Cutscenes play with sound and subtitles, and a black picture.
games.cause: The cutscenes are WebM (VP9) decoded by IMFSourceReader on a separate D3D11 device and presented by a D3D12 renderer: the frame never reaches the renderer, and a stock CrossOver 26.3 ships no demuxer that opens a WebM.
games.fix: A bridge in libxess.dll answers the shared handle of each decoded frame and carries it across to the D3D12 renderer. On CrossOver Preview 27 that is all it needs.

games.title: God of War Ragnarök
games.summary: Adaptive triggers never reach the pad: told it runs on a Steam Deck, the game never loads Sony's library and drops every trigger effect.

excerpts.note: The game's scePadSetTriggerEffect wrapper is found by the name it hands on, not by an address.
Sony's trigger effect modes become the DualSense's own trigger effect bytes.
Each effect the game builds goes to the pad, only when it changes, and the game gets the answer it always got.

games.symptom: No adaptive trigger effect on a DualSense, while the game plays its rumble and, with Steam Input on, shows PlayStation buttons.
games.cause: Steam answers that the game runs on a Steam Deck under Wine, so the game never loads Sony's library, and its scePadSetTriggerEffect wrapper drops every effect it builds.
games.fix: A jump at that wrapper sends each effect to the pad as the DualSense's own trigger effect, in an output report that carries only the trigger fields.
games.backend: D3DMetal, through NotProton; the fix does not depend on the backend.

games.title: God of War
games.summary: White specks on characters in dim light: an EQUAL depth test after a prepass, which the translated shaders do not match bit for bit.

credits.name: The author of "God Of War 2018 White Dot Fix (through Crossover)" on r/macgaming
credits.note: Found the depth test behind the white specks.

excerpts.note: Every depth state that tests EQUAL is created with the replacement test read from gow-depth-fix.ini, which removes the white specks.

games.symptom: White specks all over the characters, Kratos first, in dim light
games.cause: The G-buffer pass tests depth with EQUAL against a depth prepass, and the translated shaders do not reproduce the prepass depth to the last bit
games.fix: That depth test is created as GREATER_EQUAL
games.crossover: Preview 27, through NotProton, under Rosetta and under FEX

games.title: KINGDOM HEARTS Dream Drop Distance
games.summary: Cutscenes run with sound and a solid green picture: the luma and chroma planes never reach the game's own textures. The same DLL also swallows the shutdown fault that makes Wine open a crash dialog when a launcher or a title closes, so one install fixes both.

excerpts.note: The game asks for decode into D3D video textures; the reader gets a copy of its attributes without the two that ask for it, so it decodes in software.
The decoded NV12 frame is written straight into the luma and chroma textures the game created, so its own shader has planes to convert.

games.cause: The game opens the decoded NV12 texture in D3D12 through a shared handle and copies its two planes into textures of its own; asking D3DMetal for NV12 is fatal, and a frame in any other format leaves those planes empty, which is the solid green.
games.symptom: Cutscene runs with sound, picture solid green
games.fix: Software decode, and the luma and chroma planes written straight into the game's own plane textures
games.crossover: Stable 26.3, on a copy of it carrying this project's `winegstreamer` (2026-08-31)

games.title: Marvel's Spider-Man 2
games.summary: Characters stay in a T-pose and the symbiote breaks on M1-M4 Macs: D3DMetal reads and writes typed buffers only to element 2^28.

credits.name: macprotips
credits.note: The diagnosis, the raw views and the four rewritten shaders (public domain). MacGameFix adds a carrier that needs no DLL override and a barrier after the volumetric fog copy.

excerpts.note: macprotips': the wide R32 views past element 2^28 are created raw, which D3DMetal reads in full.
Ours: a UAV barrier after the volumetric fog copy, which removed the black blocks in the sandstorm stage.

games.symptom: Characters stay in a T-pose; the symbiote shows up as spikes, a flat black sheet, or not at all; brief black blocks flash in the opening sandstorm stage
games.cause: On M1-M4 Macs, D3DMetal returns 0 for typed buffer reads past element 2^28 and drops typed writes past it. The black blocks come from a missing barrier after the volumetric fog copy
games.fix: macprotips': the wide R32 views made raw, and four shaders rebuilt raw from your own exe. Ours: no DLL override, and a UAV barrier after `CS_VolumetricFogCopy`
games.crossover: Preview 27, through NotProton; M5 Macs do not have the limit

games.title: Mortal Kombat 11
games.summary: Has the face morph read its three-float deltas the way D3DMetal and DXMT can, which removes the dark patches, and gives the movies their colours and their frame order back. DirectX 12 and 11 alike.

credits.name: Anton Pavliuk
credits.note: Found and published first that the movie frames come out in decode order, and the reordering (MIT, DirectX 11 only); mk11-movie.c is a separate implementation.

excerpts.note: The faces. Every three-float buffer view is created as a one-float view three times as long, which D3DMetal and DXMT both read correctly; the rewritten morph shaders then read a delta's three floats one by one.
The colours. CrossOver's H.264 decoder leaves NV12 out of the types it offers, so the game took YV12 and drew it as NV12. NV12 is offered again, first.
The frame order. The decoder hands frames out in decode order; the fix holds them and hands out the one that comes first in display order.

games.symptom: Bare faces -- forehead, brows, around the eyes -- turn into smeared dark patches with hard edges that follow the light and change from frame to frame. Clean right after a screen loads, broken once the face animates; barely visible in a fight, glaring in close views, the character select and the fatalities. Masked fighters never show it. It has been there since at least an M1 Pro
games.cause: The face morph reads its per-vertex deltas from `DXGI_FORMAT_R32G32B32_FLOAT` buffer views, and D3DMetal serves those as two floats an element with z = 0
games.fix: Every such view is created as an `R32_FLOAT` view three times as long, and the two morph shaders read a delta's three floats one by one
games.backend: **D3DMetal** with D3D12 (`MK11_DX12.exe`) and **DXMT** with D3D11 (`MK11.exe`): one install covers both, whichever Steam starts
games.crossover: Preview 27 through NotProton, Game Porting Toolkit 4.0b3 (2026-10-16 and 17)

games.title: NINJA GAIDEN 3: Razor's Edge
games.summary: Will not start at all: "Insufficient VRAM. Please close all running applications." It is a Direct3D 9 title and CrossOver's DXVK cannot create a Vulkan device for it. Needs d9vk plus winevideo's DirectShow filters, applied to this executable only.

credits.name: winevideo
credits.note: Found why the movies never start (Wine's ASF Reader blocks its audio behind the video) and built the patched qasf, quartz and winegstreamer the fix installs (LGPL-2.1-or-later).

credits.name: d9vk by Sikarugir-App
credits.note: The Direct3D 9 the game runs on (zlib).

excerpts.note: The four DLLs go into the prefix's system32, its own copies kept aside, and Wine is told to load them for this game's executable only; each override is read back rather than assumed.
excerpts.code:
for d in $DLLS; do
  s="$(src_for "$d")" || { echo "error: $d is not beside this script" >&2; exit 1; }
  # Only the prefix's own file is kept aside: ours, from an earlier install,
  # is not an original to put back.
  if [ -f "$SYS/$d" ] && [ ! -f "$SYS/$d.mgvf-stock" ] && ! cmp -s "$SYS/$d" "$s"; then
    mv "$SYS/$d" "$SYS/$d.mgvf-stock"
  fi
  cp "$s" "$SYS/$d"
  echo "  $d  <- ${s#$HOME/}"
done

if [ -n "$PFX" ]; then
  for n in d3d9 qasf quartz winegstreamer; do
    # Written and then read back, as below for a bottle.
    if ! user_reg_edit "$PFX" set "$REG_KEY" "*$n" "native,builtin" \
       || ! user_reg_has_value "$PFX" "$REG_KEY" "*$n"; then
      echo "error: could not write the override for $n into $PFX/user.reg" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  done
  echo "  overrides written for this executable only, into the prefix's user.reg"

games.symptom: Will not start: "Insufficient VRAM. Please close all running applications."
games.cause: It is Direct3D 9 only, and CrossOver's DXVK cannot create a Vulkan device on MoltenVK, which offers neither transformFeedback nor timelineSemaphore. Its ASF movies never start because Wine's ASF Reader blocks the audio behind the video.
games.fix: Four DLLs in the prefix's system32 for this executable only: d9vk for Direct3D 9, and winevideo's qasf, quartz and winegstreamer for the movies. The prefix's own copies are kept aside.
games.crossover: A patched CrossOver Preview 27 (27.0.0.40921), 2026-08-28

games.title: NINJA GAIDEN 4
games.summary: The game asks Media Foundation whether anything decodes VP9 and quits if the answer is zero; on D3DMetal 4 its fences are repaired so it presents at all. Needs the staged Matroska demuxer too, except on CrossOver Preview 27, which ships it.

excerpts.note: When the engine finds no VP9 decoder, the gate the game asks Media Foundation is answered with the H.264 decoder's entry, so the game goes on and decodes in software.
On D3DMetal 4: a fence wait for a value no one has signalled yet is bridged through the CPU instead of being handed to the GPU.

games.symptom: *"Windows is missing required components… install Windows Media Foundation and the VP9 Codec. The game will now exit"* -- and it exits
games.cause: CrossOver ships no Matroska demuxer, so a WebM is recognised and then has nothing to hand off to
games.fix: Stage `libgstmatroska` beside the decoder; answer the VP9 MFT gate and decode in software
games.crossover: Stable 26.3.0.39832, measured on a stock install as well as on this project's patched engine; CrossOver Preview 27 through NotProton, with nothing staged (2026-10-14)
